chunks: 5117 - And ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “There is no cutting for open and public theft, which is snatching, but I would discipline him with taʿzīr. However, the one who takes and conceals is to have the cutting applied.”

There is no cutting for one who snatches clothes, and there is no cutting for the pickpocket if he picks from the outer garment. But if he picks from the inner garment, then cutting applies to him. There is also no cutting for a hired worker or a guest, because both are entrusted. And it has been narrated that if a guest hosts another guest and he steals, he is cut. If a paralyzed person steals, his right hand is cut in every case, whether it is paralyzed or sound. If he returns and steals again, his left foot is cut. If he returns again, he is kept permanently in prison, provision is made for him from the Bayt al-Māl of the Muslims, and he is restrained from the people.
That was narrated by al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb from al-ʿAlāʾ from Muḥammad ibn Muslim from Zurārah from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام.
And al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb also narrated it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام.
And there is no cutting for the slave if he steals from the property of his master, because it is the man’s property: one part of him has stolen from another part.

key_terms.أُعَزِّرُهُ: I administer taʿzīr, a discretionary disciplinary punishment
key_terms.الدَّغَارَةِ: open and public theft or snatching done openly
key_terms.الْخُلْسَةُ: snatching or seizing something quickly in a public manner
key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims

ai.seo_question: When is the hadd punishment of cutting applied for theft in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out detailed fiqh rulings concerning the hadd of theft, distinguishing between concealed theft and forms such as public snatching, pickpocketing from outer garments, and theft by those considered entrusted, such as workers and guests. It also addresses repeat offenses, the case of a paralyzed thief, and theft by a slave from his master’s property, showing the precision of Imamī legal treatment of criminal liability.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5117 - Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
"There is no cutting (of the hand) for open and public theft, which is snatching (Al-khulsah), but I would discipline him (ta'zir).
However, the one who steals and conceals what he takes is to have his hand cut off."

There is no cutting (of the hand) for one who snatches clothing, nor is there cutting for a pickpocket (ṭarrar) if he steals from the outer garment.
However, if he steals from the inner garment, then cutting is applied.
There is also no cutting for a worker (ajir) or a guest (ḍayf) because they are entrusted.
However, it has been narrated that if a guest hosts another guest who then steals, his hand is to be cut.
If a paralyzed person (ashall) steals, his right hand is to be cut off regardless of whether it is paralyzed or healthy. If he steals again, his left foot is to be cut off. If he steals a third time, he is to be imprisoned for life, provided for from the public treasury of the Muslims, and restrained from harming people.

This was narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Al-Alaa from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Zurarah from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), and also by Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdullah (as).
Additionally, there is no cutting for a slave if he steals from the property of his master because it is considered the wealth of the man himself, as if a part of him has stolen from another part.
